title: NVIDIA Leads the Establishment of the SAFE Working Group under OSAA to Promote AI Security Incident Sharing and Open-Source Collaboration

content_html:
The Open Security AI Alliance (OSAA), established just a week ago by NVIDIA, is rapidly advancing the AI security ecosystem. The alliance has already grown to more than 120 companies and announced the establishment of the "Shared AI Findings Exchange" (SAFE) working group, which has started collecting proposals for handling AI security incidents. The Linux Foundation is responsible for managing this initiative.

During this week's Black Hat conference, the alliance further refined its plans, focusing on aspects such as confidential reporting of AI cybersecurity incidents, notification mechanisms for affected parties, and blameless post-mortem analysis. These efforts aim to promote the sharing of security experiences and best practices within the industry.

In addition to developing collaboration standards, OSAA members continue to contribute open-source security capabilities, with plans to gradually form an open-source AI security toolchain available for enterprise deployment. This will help protect AI agents and defend against malicious AI attacks. NVIDIA provides open models and the open-source LLM vulnerability scanning tool Garak. Okta advances Agent identity technology, Red Hat develops Agent governance solutions, and Amazon contributes projects such as Strands Agents and the authorization language Cedar.

The alliance members include companies such as Adobe, BlackRock, Cisco, Intel, Microsoft, and Visa. However, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google have not yet joined. Despite this, both OpenAI and Google signed an earlier open letter initiated by NVIDIA, supported by over 200 tech companies, advocating for open-source AI.

This rapid formation of the alliance is closely related to recent discussions in the U.S. about open-source AI regulatory policies. Industry experts believe that the OSAA's accelerated progress in promoting open collaboration and security standards could further strengthen the U.S. open-source AI ecosystem and enhance AI security capabilities and industrial competitiveness through open sharing.

content_html_zh:
NVIDIA 一周前成立的开放安全人工智能联盟 (OSAA) 正在快速推进人工智能安全生态系统。 该联盟已发展到超过120家公司，并宣布成立“共享人工智能调查结果交换”（SAFE）工作组，已开始收集处理人工智能安全事件的建议。 Linux 基金会负责管理该计划。

在本周的黑帽会议上，该联盟进一步完善了计划，重点关注人工智能网络安全事件的机密报告、受影响方的通知机制以及无可指责的事后分析等方面。 这些努力旨在促进行业内安全经验和最佳实践的共享。

除了制定协作标准外，OSAA成员还持续贡献开源安全能力，计划逐步形成可供企业部署的开源AI安全工具链。 这将有助于保护人工智能代理并防御恶意人工智能攻击。 NVIDIA提供开放模型和开源LLM漏洞扫描工具Garak。 Okta 推进 Agent 身份技术，Red Hat 开发 Agent 治理解决方案，Amazon 贡献 Strands Agents 和授权语言 Cedar 等项目。

联盟成员包括 Adob​​e、BlackRock、Cisco、Intel、Microsoft 和 Visa 等公司。 不过，OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google 尚未加入。 尽管如此，OpenAI 和 Google 都签署了一份由 NVIDIA 发起、得到 200 多家科技公司支持的早期公开信，倡导开源 AI。

该联盟的迅速组建与美国近期关于开源人工智能监管政策的讨论密切相关。 业内专家认为，OSAA在推动开放协作和安全标准方面的加速进展，可以进一步强化美国开源人工智能生态系统，通过开放共享提升人工智能安全能力和产业竞争力。
